title: When to Treeify Hash Table Buckets: A Reproducible C Study of List, Hybrid, and Red-Black Tree Chaining
summary: The paper asks when C hash tables should replace long separate-chaining buckets with red-black trees, and whether hybrid-batch versus hybrid-incremental conversion timing matters as much as Java's k=8 threshold. It builds one chain_ht C API with list, hybrid-batch, hybrid-incremental, and always-tree modes, then benchmarks uniform FNV, forced-bucket stress, a same-API scale run, and trigram posting-list replay. The central result is that forced-bucket list lookups average about 31,250 comparisons while incremental hybrid or always-tree average about 15, with tree buckets using about 1.7x more heap and hybrid-batch paying large mid-load list costs.

match_target.why: This is exactly the user's target hint and the cheapest central run: list-only chaining under forced-bucket stress needs no RB-tree or hybrid conversion code while reproducing the paper's headline stress baseline.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target forced-bucket comparison count is a single-run unbounded counter with no reported std for comparisons, so use a 10% relative band (about ±3,125 comparisons around 31,250).

requirements.stmt: Implement one shared chaining API with list, always-tree, hybrid-batch, and hybrid-incremental modes behind the same insert/lookup interface.
requirements.quote: chain ht.c exposes list, always-tree, and hybrid bucket modes with either batch or incremental treeify policy behind the same insert/lookup interface

requirements.stmt: Represent each non-empty bucket as an RB tree ordered by key when using tree buckets.
requirements.quote: each non-empty bucket holds an RB tree ordered by key [10].

requirements.stmt: Use the Java-style threshold k=8 for hybrid conversion by default.
requirements.quote: Hybrid mode shares the familiar threshold k (default eight, after Java [1]), but conversion timing differs:

requirements.stmt: For hybrid-batch, insert into lists and convert eligible bins only at finalize after the load phase.
requirements.quote: inserts always go into lists; chain ht finalize converts eligible bins after the load phase

requirements.stmt: For hybrid-incremental, convert a bin to an RB tree as soon as its chain reaches k during insert.
requirements.quote: a bin converts to an RB tree as soon as its chain reaches k during insert

requirements.stmt: Build forced-bucket stress keys with an embedded bucket id and make the table hash return that id, concentrating keys into eight hot bins.
requirements.quote: keys embed a bucket id in the prefix and the table hash returns that id, concentrating keys into eight hot bins of ∼62,500 entries each

requirements.stmt: For the controlled microbenchmark, insert 500,000 unique string keys into a fixed table of 4096 buckets using FNV without resizing.
requirements.quote: Inserts 500 000 unique string keys into a fixed table of 4096 buckets using FNV (no resize).

requirements.stmt: Fix the pseudorandom seed to 1 for synthetic key generation so repetitions use the same key sequence.
requirements.cite: Appendix A.4, Datasets and workload sizes
requirements.quote: Synthetic workloads fix the pseudorandom seed (--seed 1 by default) so key sequences repeat across runs.

requirements.stmt: Count strcmp calls during chained-hash lookup and report average comparisons as comparisons divided by successful lookups.
requirements.quote: Number of strcmp calls during chained-hash lookup (chain ht)

requirements.stmt: For mid-load probes, inject lookups every 10,000 inserts using 64 random earlier keys.
requirements.quote: Table 3 adds probes during insertion (every 10,000 inserts, 64 random earlier keys).

requirements.stmt: Measure heap bytes including bucket arrays, list cells or RB nodes, and stored key strings through the chain_ht heap-bytes function.
requirements.quote: heap bytes counts bucket arrays, list cells or RB nodes, and stored key strings via chain ht heap bytes().

requirements.stmt: Do not implement Java HashMap's untreeify hysteresis, resize packaging, or Comparable tree-bin details for hybrid-incremental.
requirements.cite: Section 5.1, protocol note on Java approximation
requirements.quote: we omit untreeify hysteresis, resize packaging, and Comparable tree-bin details

requirements.stmt: For trigram replay, force one bucket per posting list of length L and insert L synthetic keys so chain length equals posting length.
requirements.quote: for each posting list of length L we force one bucket and insert L synthetic keys, so the bucket chain length equals that posting length

data.name: Synthetic uniform and forced-bucket key streams
data.how_to_get: Generate locally with the paper's repository drivers using --seed 1; no external download required.
